requiredFindings.title: A no-members walk does not implement the promised grammar-first refusal
requiredFindings.finding: A4-2 step 1 detects any malformed root purely, but then delegates the result to an ordinary walk without members and calls its result the grammar refusal. SLM does not prevalidate the whole array: _explicit_units checks each root’s grammar, then its crossings, pruning and custody before advancing to the next root (security_lifecycle_model_v1.py:683-716). With roots ["a", "../bad"] and a a physical nested repository, a no-members walk refuses JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY at a before reaching ../bad. This directly affects the existing rf2-*-grammar-after-layout case: a holds a .git file, which remains a repository boundary without the provisional-member suppression. That case currently expects JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR and A4 says its result stays unchanged. Earlier absence, bad custody or a native observation error can similarly preempt a later grammar error. Conversely, a genuinely global grammar-first rule also changes some old walk-versus-walk priorities, such as ["missing", "../bad"], so the claim that precedence changes only when a member rule and a walk refusal compete is too narrow.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Specify how the pure grammar gate returns the first malformed root’s existing PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID/JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR record, including its path, D9 and the chosen provenance, without letting a normal no-members walk replace that decision. Reuse the owning grammar and refusal shape; do not require member admission to manufacture the grammar result. Explicitly settle any array-size-versus-grammar priority and document the additional global-grammar precedence change, or narrow the promised priority consistently. Update the r4 checker and product-control requirements accordingly.
requiredFindings.validation: Retain both existing grammar-before-layout and grammar-after-layout cases under both array sources. Add mixed arrays with an earlier conventional repository, an earlier absent root and an earlier custody failure followed by malformed grammar; assert exact refusal/path/detail and the absence of item-6b observations. Include the declared array-size boundary priority. These checks must validate the selected grammar result rather than assume a no-members walk necessarily returns it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The ordering change and successor route are sound in principle
nonBlockingObservations.observation: A4 correctly rejects an unrestricted provisional-member trial before index observation: it can enter a boundary before learning that the boundary exists. Within the accepted model, which obtains gitlinks through item 6b, deciding members before descent is a sound resolution. The member-rule-first priority is permissible as an explicitly documented replacement of LD-B3B0-6, not as a claim of equivalence to r3. Binding a separately reviewed B3-b0 r4 successor before product use is the right route. This plan review does not accept the future reference or product bytes.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Preserve the scope of the short-circuit and observation obligations
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The placement/volume phase, then cap, then directory-custody plus item-6b per candidate preserves the existing cap-before-Git-read rule and the per-candidate 6b short circuit. The sentence saying no later candidate is observed should be understood in that per-candidate custody/6b phase: placement observations needed to form and count candidates still precede it. A3’s shared-ledger, retained-object binding, no-follow, custody, non-latching, scenario and access-control obligations remain. R3 must specifically fix the reopened-ancestor/evidence binding and repeated-provider-read findings; moving the walk alone does not discharge them.
